questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They can stop faster than passenger vehicles.
They need the same amount of space to turn as passenger vehicles.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and behind them. You cannot see into these areas. Stay away from them. Trucks are bigger and heavier than cars. They need more space to turn and take longer to stop.

questions.question: What size blind spots do larger vehicles have?

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: Bigger vehicles have bigger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that the driver cannot see in the side mirrors or rearview mirror.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road better.

questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see other cars, people, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, go slowly and carefully. Do not use high beams because they reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Use low beams instead to light up the road.

questions.question: When should you always use your turn signal?

options.text: When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when you enter traffic from a parking space, change lanes, or pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear to let them pass.

questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you and a right lane is open, move over. If no right lane is available, wait until the road ahead is clear and then slow down gradually to let them pass. Never brake hard because it can cause them to hit you.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require increased caution?

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well as during the day. Use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever people and vehicles are not visible from 500 feet away.

questions.question: What must other drivers allow for when driving near heavy trucks?

options.text: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop.
Heavy trucks need less distance to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks take longer to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you. Do not drive in a spot where the truck blocks your view of the road ahead.

questions.question: When can you legally pass another vehicle on the right?

options.text: When the vehicle is turning left and a passing lane is available.
If you drive off the road surface to do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is turning left and a passing lane is available.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right when a vehicle is turning left and a passing lane exists. You can also pass on the right on a road with two or more lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What must you do when you leave your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices tell you to. These devices include gates and flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you that danger is ahead. Slow down and drive with care.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They can use loudspeakers to give directions.
They can follow close behind each other.

questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances have the right-of-way when they use sirens, horns, and red or blue flashing lights. Listen to their loudspeaker instructions. Emergency vehicles often follow each other closely. Wait until you are sure the road is clear before you move.

questions.question: Which headlights should you use when driving in rain?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when it rains. High beams reflect off the rain and reduce visibility.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead is divided. Stay to the right side of the divider.

questions.question: How far ahead should you signal before turning right or left?
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. This gives other drivers time to see your signal and react. You can use your turn signal or hand and arm signals.

questions.question: What does a "No stopping" sign mean?

options.text: You can stop long enough to unload packages.
Do not stop except to obey traffic signals, police officers, or prevent a crash.
You can stop to drop off passengers.
You can stop for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop except to obey traffic signals, police officers, or prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down to reduce the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When changing lanes, which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Look for other drivers in the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and use your turn signal. Look for other drivers in the same lane. Never use your cell phone while driving to check road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when you see or hear an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Stop immediately and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop. Do this whether the emergency vehicle is coming toward you or from behind. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are breaking the law.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk your horn at crosswalks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are breaking the law.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. As a driver, always watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, when can you pass?

options.text: If you are on an expressway.
If the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass. You may only pass if the road ahead is clear and there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are the hardest to see at night because they do not have lights or reflectors like vehicles and signs do.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: You can pass at the top of a hill.
You can pass during the day only.

questions.explanation: Two solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. Oncoming traffic is heading toward you, so passing is not safe.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be allowed to legally pass the truck.

questions.explanation: Heavy trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. You should follow them carefully. Passing a truck on a hill is unsafe and illegal because you cannot see the road ahead.
